title: Before I formed thee (Jeremiah 1)
hookLine: a young man says I am a child, and God says I knew thee before

cards: He comes from a family of priests in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin. The book dates him from the thirteenth year of King Josiah until Jerusalem is carried away captive.
He's young; how young, nobody knows, since the text only lets him call himself a boy.

And he's about to be handed a hard job: to tell his own people, year after year, that disaster is coming, to watch them ignore him, and then to watch it happen. His name is Jeremiah, Jeremias in the Douay-Rheims.
And it begins with something about before he was born.

teach.b: The word of the Lord comes to him, in the Douay-Rheims: "Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee, and made thee a prophet unto the nations."
Notice the order. Known first. Then set apart.
Then given a job. Before Jeremiah did anything, he was known. His answer is honest.

teach.h: AH, AH, AH: I AM A CHILD.
teach.b: In the Douay: "Ah, ah, ah, Lord God: behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child." Stammering. God doesn't argue about his age: say not, I am a child.
You'll go where I send you. Be not afraid, for I am with thee.

teach.h: I HAVE GIVEN MY WORDS IN THY MOUTH.
teach.b: Then God touches his mouth, the way the coal touched Isaiah's lips: I have given my words in thy mouth. Then a strange little test. What do you see, Jeremiah?
A branch of an almond tree. Good, God says, for I am watching over my word. In Hebrew it's a pun: almond is shaqed, watching is shoqed.
Some readers explain the name: the almond wakes early in spring, the watchful tree. The Douay, following the Latin, simply calls it a rod watching.
The Church has taken that first line further than Jeremiah's own story: the Catechism quotes it in teaching that human life is to be respected and protected from the moment of conception.

teach.h: BEFORE I FORMED THEE, I KNEW THEE.
teach.b: For Jeremiah, the knowing came first, before all the hard years.

how: Catholics hear Jeremiah's call at Mass, and the Catechism cites Jeremiah 1:5 in its teaching on the dignity of human life from conception.

o: a shepherd's staff carried by a young prophet
almond, the branch God showed Jeremiah
a burning coal that touched a prophet's lips

p: I cannot speak, for I am a child

s: the text gives Jeremiah's exact age
it doesn't. he calls himself a child, a boy; how old he was, nobody knows.
behold, I have given my words in thy mouth.
in Hebrew, almond and watching sound alike
shaqed and shoqed: the almond is the watchful tree.

games.q: you're Jeremiah. God has just told you you're a prophet to the nations. you're young and you can't find the words. what do you say?
o: ah, ah, ah, Lord God: I cannot speak, for I am a child.
games.why: Jeremiah stammers that he's only a child. God says: say not, I am a child. be not afraid, for I am with thee.

practice: Set down, one at a time, the things you usually use to explain who you are: your job, your mistakes, your age, what people think of you. Underneath them all, Jeremiah heard something older.
If you pray, rest in his line, before I formed thee, I knew thee; if you don't, simply let yourself be for a moment, without needing to earn it.

wordCard.voice: shaqed. Hebrew for almond, the branch God showed Jeremiah as a sign that he was watching over his word. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: almond. It sounds like shoqed, watching: God watches over his word.

carryVoice: Your line: known before the womb. Known first, then set apart, then sent. Day four hundred twenty-one.
